lines.text: Listen. A father, in a Manchester flat, watches a war on the news from a country he loves. And he makes a choice — he names his unborn son after a footballer. From France.
Twenty-three years later, that son captains the midfield of Iraq... against France itself. Some stories are too perfect for any scriptwriter to dare invent. This one is true.
Welcome back to WorldCup twenty-six Legends — episode forty-four. France versus Iraq. Group I, at Stanford.
The champions of the world against the Lions of Mesopotamia. The fastest machine in football... against the boy who carries a legend's name.
France — Les Bleus. Champions in twenty-eighteen, finalists in twenty twenty-two. A team of frightening speed, depth, and ruthless quality.
Kylian Mbappé, the captain — already among the immortals, and still in his prime. One touch, and a match is over.
Michael Olise, the magician who bends defences. Ousmane Dembélé, electric and fearless. Tchouaméni and Saliba — the wall the giants break against.
Iraq — the Lions of Mesopotamia. A nation whose football was forged in the shadow of war, sanctions, and hardship most of us cannot imagine.
And at its heart, Zidane Iqbal. Born in Manchester, raised at United, named for a man from across a border — and tonight, he meets the nation of his name.
Aymen Hussein, all power and hunger up front. Ali Al-Hamadi, sharpened in England. Al-Ammari and Sulaka — eleven men carrying a country's whole heart.
So here is the duel. France's machine against Iraq's miracle. The fastest man alive... against the boy who never flinches.
Class against courage. A nation that has won it all... against a nation that has survived almost everything.
And before the goals, stay with me — because the first blow tonight does not come from the champions.
Here is how we see it. Iraq do not freeze. They believe. And Stanford is about to gasp.
The thirty-fourth minute. A corner swings in. And there — Aymen Hussein, rising above them all. The header crashes down, and in.
Iraq, one to nil. The Lions of Mesopotamia, leading the champions of the world. The stadium does not know whether to scream or cry.
And in the storm, the boy named Zidane is the calmest man on the grass. He collects, he steadies, he keeps his country's shape — just as he has since he was a child.
But this is France. And class, in the end, tells.
The sixty-first minute. Olise threads the eye of a needle, and Mbappé is gone before anyone moves — one touch, and the net rips. One apiece.
The machine has woken. And when it wakes, it does not forgive.
The eighty-seventh minute. Dembélé drives, Mbappé ghosts in behind — and the captain settles it, cold and clinical. France, two. Iraq, one.
That is our prediction — French class edging Iraqi heart, a comeback written by the immortals. The real one is yours to watch.
But the scoreline is not the story. The story is a boy who stood on the same grass as his name... and did not flinch.
In Group I, the champions survived — but Iraq made the world remember them. That is the beauty, and the cruelty, of the World Cup.
Do you agree? Comment BLEUS if France were simply too much. Comment IRAQ if the boy named Zidane was the story of the round.
And in a quiet Manchester flat, one figure watched it all, a hand over his heart. Legend number forty-four — the Namesake. The father who, in the worst of times, chose a name from across a border.
They say a name can outlive a war... and a son can carry it home. Collect him inside the game.
Which brings us to you. At worldcup twenty-six dot world, pick three of the forty-eight nations — and every goal they score, scores for you.
Free to play. Climb the leaderboard, just for fun. No prizes.

If the champions and the namesake moved you tonight, send it to a friend who believes football is bigger than borders. Hit like, subscribe — and collect Legend number forty-four, before the next legend steps from the shadows.
